source.author: verg
source.text: Optuma quaeque dies miseris mortalibus aevi prima fugit; subeunt morbi tristisque senectus et labor, et durae rapit inclementia mortis.
source.text_original: Optuma quaeque dies miseris mortalibus aevi / prima fugit; subeunt morbi tristisque senectus / et labor, et durae rapit inclementia mortis.
source.text_english: The best days of life are the first to flee from wretched mortals; diseases, sad old age, and toil come on, and the harsh severity of death carries them off.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: praepara tibi diuitias, quas cotidie eroges et numquam deficiant, dum uiget aetas, dum adhuc canis spargitur caput, antequam subeant morbi tristisque senectus et labor et durae rapiat inclementia mortis. nihil in te mediocre contentus sum: totum summum, totum perfectum desidero.
reuse.text_original: praepara tibi diuitias, quas cotidie eroges et numquam deficiant, dum uiget aetas, dum adhuc canis spargitur caput, antequam 'subeant morbi tristisque senectus et labor et durae rapiat inclementia mortis.' nihil in te mediocre contentus sum: totum summum, totum perfectum desidero.
reuse.text_english: Prepare for yourself riches that you may spend every day and never let them fail, while your age is still vigorous, while your head is still being sprinkled with gray hairs, before diseases and sad old age come on, and toil, and the harsh severity of death snatches you away. I am not content with anything in you that is mediocre: I desire the whole to be highest, the whole to be perfect.
